name: NJ-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+15 district fundamentals strongly favor Democrats
Incumbent Rob Menendez holds a large fundraising and outside-support edge
No Republican on the ballot; independent challengers report no fundraising
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95%
model.rationale: The district's fifteen-point Democratic lean, Menendez's roughly $2.2 million raised against challengers with no reported money, and the absence of a Republican nominee make a Democratic win near-certain, and markets price it around 95 percent.
model.watch: With no polling in the race, any late scandal involving the incumbent or a surge of outside spending against him is the main thing that could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Aristotle Eliopoulos is an independent standing in for the Republican side.

overview:
NJ-08 sits in heavily Democratic territory in northern New Jersey, with a partisan lean of about fifteen points toward Democrats. Incumbent Rob Menendez is running for reelection and has raised roughly $2.2 million, with about $660,000 on hand and more than $900,000 in outside support. His principal challenger, independent Aristotle Eliopoulos, reports no fundraising, and no major-party Republican appears on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and the incumbent's financial edge. Prediction markets put the Democratic win probability around 95 percent. The expected margin is about 23 points, reflecting the district's lean plus incumbency and money advantages. The absence of polling keeps confidence below what a polled Safe seat would carry, but the fundamentals point firmly to Menendez.
